title: OpenStack (orchestrator)
description: Orchestrates the per-component OpenStack blueprints into one ordered, readiness-gated install. Create one Composition of this Kind per OpenStack installation (one per namespace).

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: identity = MariaDB+Memcached+Keystone+Glance+Horizon; full = the whole catalogue, including cinder, ironic, octavia and swift, which need infrastructure you must provide yourself (a block-storage backend, a PXE interface, an lb-mgmt-net with a port per host, an RWX StorageClass): ironic, octavia and swift otherwise sit in Init forever, and cinder refuses to render while storage.backend is none; full-strict = everything except the components whose components[].requires this install does not provide, i.e. only what can start on the cluster as described (cinder joins it when storage.backend is not none). See hack/provisioning-preconditions.yaml.

enabled.title: Explicit component selection
enabled.description: Deploy exactly these components plus their transitive dependencies, overriding profile. E.g. ["heat"] also brings up keystone, rabbitmq, mariadb and memcached. Empty uses profile.

tolerations.title: Tolerations
tolerations.description: Kubernetes tolerations applied to every pod of every component (Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs and CronJobs), as each component's pod.tolerations.<component>. An explicit componentValues entry wins. E.g. a trusted-tenant vcluster's pool taint krateo.io/trusted-tenant=<namespace>:NoSchedule. Empty changes nothing.

installDefinitions.title: Register component CompositionDefinitions
installDefinitions.description: Also register each component blueprint's CompositionDefinition as the first step.

ociRepo.title: OCI chart repository
ociRepo.description: Registry path holding the per-component blueprint charts (openstack-<component>).

componentValues.title: Per-component spec overrides
componentValues.description: Per-component Composition spec overrides, by component name (an unknown name is rejected). The value at componentValues.<name> becomes that component's Composition spec, deep-merged; components without an entry use chart defaults. It is passed through here and typed by the component's own Composition CRD (generated by hack/gen-componentvalues-schema.py).

version.description: Contract version this stanza conforms to.

name.description: DNS-1123 service identifier, used as prefix for rendered resources.

owner.description: Team or contact owning this service adapter.

identity.description: Identity federation wiring: Keycloak client, optional IdP broker, and the groups mapper.

realmRef.description: Name of the KeycloakRealm CR of the owning Org. Defaults to the Org realm when omitted.

groupsMapper.description: Protocol mapper exposing group membership in tokens issued to this client.

idpBroker.description: Optional identity-provider broker this service's logins are federated through.

roleMapping.description: Mandatory map from CMP roles/capabilities to the service's native roles, reconciled by the service adapter into the native system. No service onboards without declaring it.

cmpRole.description: CMP role or capability name (see capabilities[].name / aggregateTo).

nativeRole.description: Role name in the service's native authorization system.

scope.description: Optional native scope the role binds at (e.g. project, organization, folder).

capabilities.description: Atomic, human-readable permissions this service contributes to the capability catalog. Each capability renders one aggregation-labeled ClusterRole; ABAC capabilities additionally render a Kyverno ClusterPolicy.

urlTemplate.description: Context deep-link into the service's native console. Placeholders: {org}, {tenant}, {namespace}, {project}.

preRedirect.description: Optional step executed before redirecting (e.g. native token rescoping).

mode.description: oidc-backchannel is the default; saml-slo only for SAML-only consoles.

sessionMaxTtl.description: Session TTL to keep aligned with the CMP session and downstream tokens.

usage.description: UsageRecord emission declaration. Every record implicitly carries org/tenant/service/resource dimensions plus resource tags; metrics declared here define the service-specific shape consumed uniformly by dashboards and rating.

dimensions.description: Extra per-metric dimensions beyond the implicit org/tenant/service/resource/tags.

health.description: Normalized health emission. The adapter must map the native signal onto exactly: OK | Warning | Critical | Unknown.

type.description: endpoint: probe an HTTPS endpoint; metric: derive from emitted usage metrics; adapter: the adapter computes it natively.

tagging.description: Tag support declaration. Non-tag-native services are tracked in the shared tag registry; remediation declares whether the adapter can patch tags on existing resources.

native.description: Whether the underlying service supports tags/labels natively.

remediation.description: Whether the adapter can patch tags on existing resources (used by governance remediation).

keyPattern.description: Optional regex constraining tag keys accepted by the native system.

ticketing.description: Support-ticket classification and routing hints for tickets opened in the context of this service.

serviceContract.description: Service integration descriptor (contract v1): identity federation, role mapping, capabilities, SSO deep-link, usage/health, tagging, ticketing. Chart defaults are authoritative; deployments override only environment-specific fields (URLs, realm).

contractEmitter.title: Removed in 0.3.68
contractEmitter.description: The contract emitter was removed in 0.3.68: the CMP's usage and health emitter is krateo-platformops/cmp-usage-collector. Only enabled: false is accepted, so a Composition created before 0.3.68 keeps validating.

enabled.description: Removed in 0.3.68; must be false or absent.

rerunHooks.title: Re-run a component's hooks
rerunHooks.description: A token per component name (an unknown name is rejected). Setting or changing rerunHooks.<component> passes it to that component alone, as its krateo.rerunHooksToken: its values change, so core-provider runs a real helm upgrade, which runs every hook again. Use the current time. README: "A component reads Ready=False/HooksMayNotHaveRun" (#297).

publicEndpoints.title: Public endpoints
publicEndpoints.description: The OpenStack APIs, Horizon and the noVNC console over HTTPS from outside the cluster, through one Gateway API Gateway with an HTTPRoute per public endpoint of a selected component, a cert-manager Certificate and an ingress NetworkPolicy for the namespace (#311). Each component's public catalog endpoint becomes https://<service>.<baseDomain>; Horizon becomes ClusterIP with Secure cookies. Needs a Gateway API implementation and cert-manager (Krateo: features.ingress); refused on a live cluster without their CRDs. Off (the default) changes nothing. README: "Public endpoints".

enabled.description: Render the Gateway, routes, Certificate and NetworkPolicy, and move every selected component's public endpoint to its hostname.

baseDomain.description: Every public hostname is <service>.<baseDomain>, e.g. keystone.cloud.example.com. Required when enabled.

gatewayClassName.description: The GatewayClass of the Gateway API implementation (agentgateway is what Krateo's features.ingress installs).

name.description: The Gateway's name; its certificate Secret is <name>-tls and each route <name>-<service>.

addresses.description: Reserved IP addresses for the Gateway, so a rebuild keeps its DNS records valid. Empty: the implementation assigns one.

name.description: The cert-manager issuer of the Gateway's certificate, e.g. krateo-selfsigned-ca. Required when enabled.

maxAge.description: Strict-Transport-Security max-age (seconds) on every HTTPS response.

enabled.description: Deny ingress to the namespace by default; allow the namespace itself, the nodes, the Gateway and allowNamespaces.

nodeCIDRs.description: The CIDRs of the nodes' own addresses. Required with networkPolicy.enabled: the hostNetwork data-plane pods reach RabbitMQ and the APIs from them.

allowNamespaces.description: Namespaces whose pods may reach this namespace (e.g. the OpenStack KOG operators'). Empty: none.

proxyNamespace.description: Where the implementation runs the Gateway's proxy pods (selected by gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name). Empty: the install namespace.

compute.title: Compute
compute.description: virtType: qemu (software emulation, the default) or kvm (hardware virtualization: nova virt_type kvm and cpu_mode host-model, libvirt to match, and libvirt refuses to start on a node without /dev/kvm). README "Running guests on KVM" (#303).

kogCredentials.title: Credentials for Krateo KOG operators
kogCredentials.description: Opt-in. enabled renders, in the release's namespace (cross-namespace is not supported yet), openstack-kog-clouds (a clouds.yaml for the keystone-, neutron- and glance-kog auth proxies), openstack-kog-token (an admin token for nova-kog, re-minted every 6 h) and openstack-kog-endpoints (nova's and keystone's internal URLs and the region, no secret), all from the install's generated admin root. README "Driving this OpenStack with Krateo KOG operators" (#303).

storage.title: Storage backend
storage.description: The backend that provides block storage, the `block-storage` capability cinder requires (#196, #308). Profile full-strict selects cinder only when storage.backend is not none, and the umbrella passes the value to each as its krateo.storageBackend (a componentValues override of that key is refused). With none, a cinder selected anyway (profile full, or enabled) refuses to render, naming this value. With a ceph backend the install consumes Ceph through copies of the keys Ceph mints (storage.ceph), never client.admin. See hack/provisioning-preconditions.yaml.

ceph.title: Ceph consumer
ceph.description: How the install consumes Ceph when storage.backend is ceph-rook or ceph-external (#308): each client key and the monitor addresses are copied by External Secrets Operator from where Ceph keeps them, and the charts project the copies. No client.admin key is read anywhere.

sourceNamespace.description: Where the client-key and mon_host Secrets live; empty: this release's namespace. For ceph-rook, the CephCluster's namespace (its owner grants the copy store read access).

clients.description: The Ceph user each consumer authenticates as (client.<name>); for ceph-rook, the CephClient name.

cinder.description: cinder-volume's user, also libvirt's for attached volumes.

rook.description: Where Rook keeps the keys and monitors (ceph-rook).

clientKey.description: The key holding a CephClient's key.

keys.description: The operator-named Secrets (ceph-external); each secret is required with ceph-external.

monHost.description: The monitor addresses, as ceph.conf's mon_host.

pools.description: The RBD pools, created where the users are (a CephBlockPool, or the Ceph admin).

libvirtSecretUUID.description: The libvirt secret every hypervisor defines for cinder's user, passed to cinder, libvirt and nova.

glanceStore.description: pvc keeps images on glance's volume; rbd stores them in the images pool.

glanceImagesMigrated.description: With glanceStore rbd on an install whose images are on the glance-images claim, glance refuses until this is true: copy the images to the rbd store first, or confirm there is none to keep.

backend.title: Block-storage backend
backend.description: none = no backend (the default): profile full-strict leaves cinder out, and a cinder selected anyway refuses to render, naming this value; ceph-rook = Ceph run by Rook, whose CephClients mint the client keys (#308); storage.ceph says where; ceph-external = an existing Ceph whose admin creates the users and places their keys (#308); storage.ceph.keys names each Secret.

ha.title: High availability
ha.description: Opt-in (#309). enabled runs memcached as 3 replicas behind a headless Service, with every component listing each replica in its memcache server list, and refuses the render while fewer than 3 nodes carry openstack-control-plane=enabled (when the orchestrator can read nodes). Off changes nothing. README "High availability".

title.description: Human-readable permission shown in the role composer.

enforcement.description: Enforcement layer: rbac = Kubernetes RBAC only; acr = auth-strength/step-up on top of RBAC; cross-org = central parent-realm role; abac = attribute/conditional rule (Kyverno CEL) on top of RBAC.

requiresAcr.description: ACR/LoA the caller's token must satisfy (step-up is triggered otherwise). Required when enforcement is 'acr'.

crossOrgRole.description: Central parent-realm role backing this capability. Required when enforcement is 'cross-org'.

aggregateTo.description: Predefined roles this capability aggregates into (rendered as rbac.krateo.io/aggregate-to-<role> labels).

abac.description: Attribute/conditional rule rendered as a Kyverno ClusterPolicy (CEL). Required when enforcement is 'abac'.
